# Seed sweep of every property test

*12 October 2026. Report only: no code, test or spec changed. Branch `claude/seed-sweep-2026-10-12`, from main at `5892211`. Test identities only.*

## In plain words

Six tests in the repository make up random histories and check the library's answers against the rules. Which histories they make depends on a random number, the seed, drawn at the start of each run. The last two failures on main (`docs/invariant-deal-promises-fix.md`, `docs/closing-owes-fix.md`) showed up only under particular seeds.

So each of the six was run with the same 300 seeds, 1,800 runs in all. **Every run passed. Nothing failed, so there is no cause to judge and no question for Nobody, allegedly.**

## Which tests draw a seed

Searched across the Rust and TypeScript sources and the scripts for `AGREEMENTS_INVARIANT_SEED`, `LAW_INVARIANT_SEED`, any other `…_SEED` variable, `proptest`, and other random generators.

The six properties, all in `core/tests/agreements_invariants.rs`, all seeded through its `seed()` (`AGREEMENTS_INVARIANT_SEED`, or the older `LAW_INVARIANT_SEED`):

| Property | Default cases |
|---|---|
| `collective_promises_hold` | 48 |
| `leftovers_ignore_the_order_of_holders` | 2000 |
| `collective_verdicts_do_not_depend_on_order` | 24 |
| `deal_promises_hold` | 48 |
| `deal_verdicts_do_not_depend_on_order` | 24 |
| `collective_stakes_move_only_with_their_holders` | 96 |

Left out, and why:

- **`verifier2_export`** (`verifier2/export/export.rs`, included in the same test file). It reads `VERIFIER2_SEED`, but it is ignored by default, its seed defaults to 1 rather than a random draw, and it checks nothing: it writes histories and verdicts for verifier2 to compare.
- **`core/tests/law_invariants.rs`** no longer exists on main; it became `agreements_invariants.rs` in the rename.
- **TypeScript.** No property tests. The only random draws (`clients/collective/test/access.test.ts`, `clients/genesis/test/cli.test.ts`) pick a local test port, not a history.

## How it was run

- Main at `5892211`, tree clean before, during and after. The tree was not touched while runs were going.
- One release build: `cargo test -p mor-core --release --test agreements_invariants --no-run` (rustc 1.97.0). The built test binary was then run directly from `core/`, as `cargo test` does, once per property and seed, four at a time.
- Each run set only `AGREEMENTS_INVARIANT_SEED`, so each property ran with its default case count.
- Each run's log was checked: it names the expected property, seed and case count, and ends "1 passed; 0 failed".
- Total test time across all runs: about 2,720 seconds.

The replay command for any one run, in a release build:

```
AGREEMENTS_INVARIANT_SEED=<seed> cargo test -p mor-core --release --test agreements_invariants -- --exact <property> --nocapture
```

## Results

| Property | Seeds | Passed | Failed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `collective_promises_hold` | 300 | 300 | 0 |
| `leftovers_ignore_the_order_of_holders` | 300 | 300 | 0 |
| `collective_verdicts_do_not_depend_on_order` | 300 | 300 | 0 |
| `deal_promises_hold` | 300 | 300 | 0 |
| `deal_verdicts_do_not_depend_on_order` | 300 | 300 | 0 |
| `collective_stakes_move_only_with_their_holders` | 300 | 300 | 0 |
| **All** | | **1,800** | **0** |

In cases, not runs: 14,400 histories for each of the two promise properties, 7,200 for each order property, 28,800 for the stakes property, and 600,000 for the leftovers property.

Since nothing failed, no rule of Agreements draft 11 had to be read to judge a cause.

*What this does not show:* passing 300 seeds at the default case counts does not mean no seed fails. The two earlier failures were each one seed among many that passed. Longer runs (more cases per seed) reach longer histories and are the next step if wanted.
